newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-POOR RESULTS GIVE PSG CAUSE FOR CONCERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POOR RESULTS GIVE PSG CAUSE FOR CONCERN.

text.p: Paris St Germain's potential for winning the French league title and retaining the European Cup Winners' Cup has been undermined by two poor results in the last few days.
The worries began last Thursday when they were beaten 4-2 in Istanbul by Galatasaray in the first leg of their second round Cup Winners' Cup tie.
Then on Sunday they allowed champions Auxerre to battle back and steal a 1-1 draw in a French league match by grabbing a last minute penalty after PSG visbily tired towards the end of the game.
"I'm not disappointed because we did our best and a draw with Auxerre is nothing humiliating," said PSG's Brazilian manager Ricardo. "You just can't always win."

Although it is too early to talk about a crisis as PSG still have a six-point lead over second-placed Monaco and are seven points ahead of Auxerre, they no longer have an air of invincibility about them.
At the same time both Monaco and Auxerre seem capable of mounting equally realistic title challenges.
"With three points for a win, things can change very fast," warned Auxerre midfielder Philippe Violeau. "The fight for the title will be a tough one and we still stand a chance."
Ricardo is also confident of a quick return to form.
"For four or five matches, we have had quite a few key players injured," he said, adding: "Now they are coming back. And let's not forget that we are still undefeated after 13 league matches."

For both the Auxerre and Galatasaray matches, PSG badly missed international goalkeeper Bernard Lama, out of action for several weeks with a knee injury, but who should be back for their next match at Rennes on Friday.

In Istanbul, they were without Brazilian World Cup star Leonardo, arguably their best player this season, who was away on international duty, while against Auxerre, PSG were without defenders Bruno N'Gotty, who has a calf injury, and Alain Roche, who was suspended.
But the worries are not just centered on PSG's own form, for while they are wavering slightly, Monaco are playing very well.
Monaco beat Borussia Moenchengladbach 4-2 in Germany in a UEFA Cup match last week and went on to crush Nice 4-1 on Saturday.

"We score plenty of goals at the moment and that's very encouraging," said Monaco trainer, former international midifielder Jean Tigana. "Paris are a strong side and must be regarded as the favourites but there's a long way to go yet."
